page: Microsoft Azure D160als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dalsv7 server family. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration provides 160 vCPUs derived from 80 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 320.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core.

This server type does not include any local storage, meaning all storage operations rely on external, network-attached options, though it is premium storage capable. It does not feature any graphical processing units. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptography standards such as AES and SHA_NI, which accelerate vector calculations and secure operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the D160als_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core CPU stress tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 14528.43 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 463.81 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The server also excels in data processing, achieving 202.7 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 113.82 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, the primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which may limit its suitability for memory-intensive database workloads that require massive in-memory caching.

Given its high compute density and strong performance in multi-threaded tasks, the D160als_v7 is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads. These include large-scale software compilation, ray tracing, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based large language model inference, where it achieves top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds.
